title: Hosted Endpoint Bundle: Gated Launch PRD + Staged Acceptance Checklist
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: This ticket contains the product requirements document (PRD), clarified scope, acceptance criteria and a staged launch checklist for a bundled hosted endpoint surface that exposes chat, completions, embeddings and reranking as a cohesive family. The primary goal is to deliver a single predictable developer experience that preserves per-capability contracts while introducing adaptive fallbacks, behavioral quality gates and a canary rollout plan. The PRD emphasizes backward-compatible contracts, telemetry and automated rollback triggers tied to quality regressions measured on canonical eval sets.
scope_included: Unified API surface for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank under a single endpoint family (versioned)
Streaming for chat and completions with chunked deltas and content-metadata headers
Embeddings: batched create API with per-model dimensionality transparency
Rerank: lightweight rerank endpoint with top-K scoring and stability guarantees
Adaptive fallback policy: automatic model variant downgrade (quantized or smaller model) when capacity or latency SLOs are at risk
Quality gating: automated evaluation against shared prompt suites before increasing rollout percentage
Observability: per-route SLO dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, prompt/response sampling for privacy-safe manual review
SDK surface: parity for Python and TypeScript SDKs for the new bundle
Docs: new quickstarts, migration guide, and contract examples for structured outputs
scope_excluded: Dedicated/reserved capacity UI changes (separate Dedicated product work)
On-prem private deployment packaging (to be covered by private deployment roadmap)
Large-scale model onboarding beyond the curated model list for launch
Deep multimodal primitives (image/video) for this initial bundle
requirements: API contract must support explicit capability parameter and auto-detection for legacy clients
Streaming responses must include finalization tokens and stable delta ordering
Backwards-compatible schema for existing chat and completion routes; deprecated flags must be supported for one release cycle
Embeddings must expose model id and vector dimensionality in response metadata
Rerank must guarantee deterministic scoring for identical input order and seed
Latency SLOs: p99 <= 350ms for stable small-sequence completions (regional), p95 <= 850ms for chat with streaming enabled
Availability SLO: 99.9% regional availability for the hosted bundle on GA
Quality regression threshold: automatic halt of rollout if evaluation A/B relative quality drop > 3% on primary prompt set
Cost controls: per-token cost estimation surfaced in response metadata and console
RBAC and audit logging enabled for endpoint operations and rollout events
Canary and rollout APIs: support percentage-based traffic splits, manual promote/rollback, and automatic rollback triggers
api_contracts: /v1/hosted/generate - unified generate route with 'capability' param: chat|completion|embedding|rerank
/v1/hosted/stream - streaming websocket/HTTP2 with chunked JSON deltas and 'is_final' flag
Common fields: model, model_variant, client_request_id, metadata.tags
Embeddings response: {embedding, model, dims, model_variant, request_id}
Rerank response: {scores: [{id, score}], top_k, model_variant, request_id}
Error semantics: stable error codes for rate-limit/backpressure/service-unavailable with recommended retry-after header
acceptance_criteria: Contract tests: all existing hosted API contract test suites pass against the new endpoint family with no breaking changes for legacy clients
SDKs: Python and TS SDKs integrate the unified routes; official examples updated and pass smoke tests
Performance: baseline benchmark (internal runner) shows no regression >5% in throughput and p95 latency across representative workloads compared to previous separate endpoints
Quality: regression tests (eval harness) show model output quality within +/-2% of previously measured baselines across 3 canonical prompt suites per capability
Fallback correctness: when simulated capacity constraints are injected, 100% of routed requests are sent to compatible variants and responses include fallback metadata
Observability: new dashboards show per-capability SLOs, rollout percent, error budget burn rate and token cost breakdown; alerting configured for SLO breach
Security: SSO-configured customers able to limit access by RBAC rules; audit events recorded for rollout actions
Docs and migration guide published and linked from console before GA
Runbook: runbook for rollback and degraded-mode operation validated in a tabletop exercise
Canary: staged canary passes automated quality gates at 0%, 1%, 5% and 25% before GA expansion
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Internal dogfood: 100% internal traffic for 1 week; internal-onboarding checklist completed
Phase 1 - Private preview: select customers (10 orgs) on request with manual rollout control; collect feedback and telemetry for 3 weeks
Phase 2 - Gradual canary: automated rollout percentages at 0%->1%->5%->25% with evaluation gates after each step
Phase 3 - Regional GA: enable in us-west1/us-east1/europe-west1; monitor SLOs for 72h pre-expansion
Phase 4 - Full GA: open to self-serve, update pricing docs and quotas; announce via changelog and blog post
launch_checklist: PRD sign-off by PM, Eng, Design and Security
All contract tests pass in staging and prod candidate cluster
Streaming API load tests meet throughput targets at 95th percentile
SDK release notes and packages published (Python, TS) and validated in example apps
Docs: API reference, quickstarts, migration guide, and structured-output examples published
Telemetry: dashboards and alerts configured and tested; sampling rules verified for privacy compliance
Runbook: incident runbooks and rollback playbooks documented and reviewed
Legal & compliance: security questionnaire updated; data retention and KMS behavior documented
Pricing & quotas: per-capability quotas configured and billing integration validated
Support readiness: playbook for customer requests, escalation paths and SLA expectations distributed
Canary automation: traffic-split tooling validated and auto-rollback triggers enabled
Accessibility & UX: Console changes verified by design and QA
Load: production-like replay tests completed for peak-hour token throughput
Post-launch monitoring: 72h heightened monitoring window scheduled with on-call coverage
risks_mitigations: Risk: Quality regression after fallback or model variant change -> Mitigation: block rollout if eval delta >3% and require manual triage
Risk: Unexpected token-cost spikes -> Mitigation: circuit-breaker on token-cost per-request and emergency rate-limits
Risk: Streaming reorder or partial-finalization bugs -> Mitigation: strict streaming contract tests and end-to-end harness for consumer SDKs
Risk: RBAC/audit gaps -> Mitigation: pre-launch security review, pen-test checklist and audit log validation
Risk: SDK adoption friction -> Mitigation: maintain legacy path and provide migration quickstart + compatibility flags for one release
